IB

IB Computer Science

Explore the course by theme, topic, and subtopic.

IB Computer Science is a two-year course in which students study how computer systems work, how software is designed, and how computational thinking is used to solve real problems. The course combines theory with practical problem-solving and programming, and is organised into two main areas: Concepts of computer science and Computational thinking and problem-solving. It is available at both Standard Level (SL) and Higher Level (HL).

What You Study

The course is split into two themes.

Theme A

Concepts of Computer Science

This part of the course focuses on the theory behind computer systems, including how computers process data, how networks communicate, how databases are designed and queried, and how machine learning systems are developed and evaluated.

A1

Computer Fundamentals

Core principles that underpin the operation of a computer system.

  • A1.1 Computer hardware and operation
  • A1.2 Data representation and computer logic
  • A1.3 Operating systems and control systems
  • A1.4 Translation HL
SL: 11h | HL: 18h
A2

Networks

How computers communicate and how modern networks are structured and secured.

  • A2.1 Network fundamentals
  • A2.2 Network architecture
  • A2.3 Data transmissions
  • A2.4 Network security
SL: 11h | HL: 18h
A3

Databases

The storage, organisation and retrieval of data.

  • A3.1 Database fundamentals
  • A3.2 Database design
  • A3.3 Database programming
  • A3.4 Alternative databases HL
SL: 11h | HL: 18h
A4

Machine Learning

Machine learning and the issues involved in building and using ML systems.

  • A4.1 ML fundamentals
  • A4.2 Data preprocessing HL
  • A4.3 ML approaches HL
  • A4.4 Ethical considerations
SL: 5h | HL: 18h

Theme B

Computational Thinking and Problem-Solving

This part of the course focuses more directly on designing solutions, writing programs, and using computational thinking to analyse and solve problems.

B1

Computational Thinking

The ways computer scientists think about problems and solutions.

  • B1.1 Approaches to computational thinking
SL: 5h | HL: 5h
B2

Programming

The largest part of the course — practical programming knowledge.

  • B2.1 Programming fundamentals
  • B2.2 Data structures
  • B2.3 Programming constructs
  • B2.4 Programming algorithms
  • B2.5 File processing
SL: 40h | HL: 42h
B3

Object-Oriented Programming

Object-oriented design and programming.

  • B3.1 Fundamentals of OOP for a single class
  • B3.2 OOP for multiple classes HL
SL: 7h | HL: 23h
B4

Abstract Data Types

Linked lists, binary search trees, sets and hashing.

  • B4.1 Fundamentals of ADTs HL
HL Only | 23h

Assessment

The course is assessed through external examinations and one internal assessment task. At SL, external assessment is 70% and IA is 30%. At HL, external is 80% and IA is 20%.

Paper 1

Based on Theme A and the pre-seen case study.

SL1h 15m — 35%
HL2h — 40%

Paper 2

Based on Theme B.

SL1h 15m — 35%
HL2h — 40%

Internal Assessment

The computational solution — a practical project.

SL30%
HL20%

Case Study

Pre-seen scenario — research in advance, answer in Paper 1.

Extended Essay

Independent research. Optional.

In Summary

IB Computer Science covers computer systems, networks, databases, machine learning, computational thinking, programming, OOP and, at HL, abstract data types. Assessment is split between two exam papers and one practical internal assessment.
